# Errors

Every I/O method returns `Result<T, runtime::Error>`. An `Err` is either a
transport failure or a non-2xx response after the network layer's retries
(exponential backoff + jitter, `401` refresh, `Retry-After`). For a non-2xx
response, `err.status()` is the HTTP status and `err.api()` the
`runtime::ApiError` with Box's error `code`, `message`, and `request_id`
plus the raw `body`; both are `None` for any other failure:

```rust,ignore
match result {
    Err(err) if err.status() == Some(404) => { /* not found */ }
    Err(err) => eprintln!("{err}"), // e.g. box: status 403 access_denied: … (request_id …)
    Ok(value) => { /* … */ }
}
```

## Etags: `If-None-Match` and `If-Match`

Files and folders carry an `etag`. Send it back to stay in sync with Box
(Box's [Ensure consistency](https://developer.box.com/guides/api-calls/ensure-consistency/)
guide):

- **Reads** — a file or folder `get`, and each shared-item lookup, has an
  `…_if_modified` variant that takes the stored etag, sends it as
  `If-None-Match`, and returns `Ok(None)` when Box answers `304 Not Modified`:
  keep your cached copy. (The plain method surfaces that 304 as the error
  above if you set `if-none-match` on it yourself.)
- **Writes** — pass the etag as `if_match` on a file or folder update or
  delete, or a new file version upload. Box answers `412 Precondition
  Failed` (code `precondition_failed`) when the item changed since you read
  it: read it again, reapply your change, retry. `If-Match` can't block a move.

```rust,ignore
match client.files.get_if_modified(file_id.clone(), etag.clone(), None).await? {
    None => { /* unchanged since etag */ }
    Some(file) => { /* changed: the current file */ }
}
let guarded = FilesUpdateOptions { if_match: Some(etag), ..Default::default() };
if let Err(err) = client.files.update(file_id, body, Some(guarded)).await {
    if err.status() == Some(412) { /* changed since etag: re-read and retry */ }
}
```
